schema_note: This file is not valid against contracts/participant-observation.schema.json. That schema requires case_id, participant_id, artifact_revision and observed, and sets additionalProperties false, so it admits none of the six top-level keys the landing gate reads. method.isolation: Isolated full clone (git clone --no-hardlinks of the repository root into a session scratch directory), detached at the pinned commit. git status --porcelain empty before and after every command. Nothing in the subject was edited, staged, committed, merged, reset or rebased. All mutation testing ran on in-memory copies or throwaway files inside the scratch directory.
method.independence_from_the_package: Claim 1 was measured by rendering, not by reading source and not with this package's readers. I wrote my own harness that compiles each of the 23 files in .claude/workflows/ as an async function body with recording stubs for the four host primitives (agent, parallel, pipeline, phase, log) and a JSON-schema-driven return generator, then captured every agent() dispatch actually reached and its prompt string. sov-loop.js was driven down both of its branches (evidence_mode true and false) with hand-built envelopes; sov-review.js needed a pipeline(items, map, reduce) stub to reach its dispatches.
method.second_independent_oracle: node v22.22.2 --check was used as an external oracle for the question 'is this legal JavaScript', so that the package's own lexer never graded its own corpus.
method.known_limit: My renderer models the host's execution as a wrapped async function body with those primitives injected. That model is inferred from the files, not verified against the Claude Code host. Every prior reading carries the same unverified assumption and says so.

dissented.claim_attacked: Claim 2 - the twenty-nine constructions are an executable corpus that demonstrates what it says.
dissented.finding: Case D18's mutation is not valid JavaScript. It is refused, but as broken source, not as the scan desynchronisation it claims to show; and the refusal it is presented as covering has no case in the corpus at all.
dissented.mechanism: D18 replaces phase('Select') with a block ending `arrD[0]\n/"/.test(hitD)`. Under JavaScript's own ASI rules that is `arrD[0] / "/.test(hitD)`, leaving a double-quoted string unterminated. audit.violations reaches unreadable(source) first, returns 'not readable JavaScript: line 240: a " string is not closed before the line ends', and `continue`s - so scan_is_stable is never called for that file.
dissented.external_oracle: node --check refuses the D18 mutation with 'SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token' at that line. It accepts all 28 other mutations and all 23 live workflows. The package's own lexer was not the judge of this.
dissented.measured_gap: I instrumented every case: zero of the twenty-nine drives scan_is_stable to False, and zero drives the frame's block count below six. So two refusal branches of audit.violations - 'what this file is read to contain depends on whether a `/` is division or a regex' and 'witnessFrame renders N block(s); the frame is gone' - have no defeating case. Three more have none: 'the frame no longer carries the builder's account at all', 'CONTRACT/CHECKS reaches the evaluator after the account', and the SCOPE/CHECKS/STATE variants of the missing-block and moved-phrase rules (only the SUBJECT variants are exercised, by D03 and D09).
dissented.the_branch_is_live_and_reachable: I built the legal version D18 should have been: `const aP=[4]; const qP = aP[0] / 2 + '/'`. node accepts it, the lexer accepts it, scan_is_stable returns False, and audit.violations emits exactly the intended message. The refusal works. Nothing in the shipped corpus proves it.
dissented.why_it_matters: SDLC.md gate 3 and AGENTS.md Testing and verification require a defeating case per consequential behaviour. The commit message says all twenty-nine constructions run 'through one predicate in both directions'. One of them does not demonstrate its own subject, and the corpus reads as coverage of a branch it never reaches. That is the defect this concern is about, arriving one level up, which is the same sentence the test module uses about itself.

dissented.claim_attacked: Claim 2 - the corpus demonstrates what each case says it demonstrates.

dissented.mechanism: scripts/tests/test_witness_context_defeats.py: `if not violations(mutated(case)): survived.append(...)`. TheCorpusIsWellFormed grades id, found_by_reading, shows, file and the presence of a mutation - never the relation between `shows` and the message produced.
dissented.evidence: I captured the actual violation for all twenty-nine. D18's is a lexer verdict, not a scan verdict. D16's message reads 'a dispatch declares an agent type this cannot read once' for a dispatch that declares no agentType at all. D17 emits two violations, one of them against an unrelated `agent('build', OPTSB)` worker dispatch that the mutation collaterally made unreadable.

dissented.claim_attacked: Claim 3 - scan.py is the single mask for the package and no reader keeps a private scanner that disagrees with it.
dissented.finding: scripts/sovprompts/render.py keeps its own scanner. `_literals` has private comment and string handling with no regex or template-literal awareness, and `blocks` has a second private quote/bracket/comma splitter. calls.py and dispatch.py both import render._literals, so the private reader is load-bearing across the package. It disagrees with scan.masked on legal JavaScript, and one disagreement is an uncaught exception rather than a refusal.
demonstrations_on_legal_javascript: A `//` comment containing a comma inside witnessFrame's return array - `// ordering note, load-bearing` - splits the array at that comma. audit.violations returns two false convictions on an otherwise unchanged frame: 'the frame opens on '', not the subject' and 'the frame has no SUBJECT block'. node --check accepts the file; nothing an agent reads has changed.

A `/* first, always */` block comment before the SUBJECT element raises render.Unreadable('unterminated comment') out of blocks(), through _frame_violations, and out of audit.violations, which has no handler. The check does not refuse - it errors. scripts/tests/test_witness_context_provenance.py calls blocks() the same way and would error with it.

Rewriting one frame block as a template literal, with identical rendered text, produces 'the frame has no SCOPE block'. scan.py handles template literals by construction; render.py has no backtick branch.
Controls: the same comments without a comma pass; the unmodified file passes.
dissented.docstring_graded_as_a_claim: render.py states 'Anything built another way is reported as unreadable rather than silently passing.' It is not reported. It escapes as an exception. The module docstrings across this package were rewritten each time they were defeated and this one is false in the same way its predecessors were.
dissented.counted: Four independent lexical readers now exist: scan.masked, lexer.tokens (its own tokenizer, importing only BEFORE_REGEX_WORDS), render._literals, and blocks' comma splitter. The commit message's narrower claim - that bindings._without_strings and the enumerator consume the mask, and lexer takes its disambiguation words from it - is true. Claim 3 as put to me is not.

SDLC.md Release gate item 6 is written about a Red engagement. This candidate generalises it to every sov-witness dispatch in the harness. The generalisation is sound in spirit and is an extension of the governing text rather than a literal enforcement of it. The seventh reading recorded the same thing; it remains unsettled and is not mine to settle.

My renderer's model of the host execution environment is inferred from the workflow files and unverified against the Claude Code host. Every reading of this concern, including this one, rests on that model.

is_this_a_coherent_design: Partly, and the honest answer is that its centre is coherent and its edges are an accumulation. Three things in this candidate are genuine structure: one mask consumed by the readers that do consume it, one predicate read in both directions, and a corpus that puts refusals in the tree instead of in docstrings. Those are the right moves and they hold. What sits around them is the accumulation: four lexical readers rather than one, a repo-wide rule that grades presence while the frame rule grades position, an enumerator that fails closed on the type and open on the callee, and a corpus that counts refusals instead of identifying them. Each of the twenty-nine cases closes the construction it names, and D1, D4 and D5 are each the next hop out from a case already in the corpus. That is what an accumulation looks like from inside: every step is a real repair and the class survives. The measurable test of the sixth reading's judgement is D5 - the frame not being the only producer is what leaves the presence rule as the only rule twenty workflows have, and two lines defeat it.
standing_note: This observation supports no standing transition. It is an observation, not a settlement and not a ratification, and verdict DISSENTED does not permit a landing. Had the reading gone the other way the most it could support is OPEN -> BUILT or BUILT -> WITNESSED; only Bdo ratifies.
judgement_items: Does SDLC.md Release gate item 6, written for a Red engagement, govern every sov-witness dispatch in the harness? This candidate and its predecessors read it as generally binding. Two readings have now recorded the extension as sound in spirit and not literal. Only the seat that owns SDLC.md can settle whether the harness-wide reading is the rule or an analogy, and the answer changes what the three unframed dispatches mean.

Should the landing gate's current_base_commit resolve the remote main rather than a local ref? That decision changes whether a frozen candidate whose base is twelve commits behind the releasable System of Record can land, and it is a policy about what 'current base' names, not an engineering choice inside this concern.
